title: Event-safety signal layer and resumable-stream semantics for Python SDK streaming chat
creator: Jordan Patel
description:
Summary: Implement a dedicated 'event-safety' signal layer in the Python SDK streaming surface to separate moderation/safety events and non-final token fragments from committed output. Provide resumable-stream semantics and deterministic retry behavior so client apps can safely continue or retry streams without showing duplicate or unsafe content.

Motivation: Current streaming chat signals mix partial tokens, tool calls, and safety moderation notices in the same message stream. That makes it hard for developers to reliably decide what to render to users vs buffer as ephemeral data, and complicates retries: if a stream is retried after a mid-stream safety block, apps currently face duplication or unclear repair points. This ticket designs an explicit signal layer plus helper APIs that produce clear checkpoints and idempotent resume tokens, improving developer ergonomics and reducing customer impact when retries or model fallbacks occur.

Goals and constraints:
- Introduce a separate event type 'safety' emitted alongside token/fragment events. Safety events are out-of-band and must not be stitched into final text unless the app opts in after review.
- Define 'commit' boundaries: SDK will expose checkpoint tokens (sequence IDs + HMAC signatures) representing safe resume points. These checkpoints are stable across retries and model-variant fallbacks.
- Provide high-level streaming helper: StreamingChatSession. It exposes: on_event(callback), checkpoint(), resume(checkpoint_token), and finalize(). Works sync and async.
- Keep the wire protocol backward-compatible: servers may continue to send existing event envelopes; SDK maps legacy events into the new layered representation.
- Minimal latency impact: checkpointing must be lightweight and incremental (no full transcript hashing on each token).
- Telemetry: emit events for safety triggers, resume attempts, duplicate-suppression actions, and commit latencies.

API proposal (Python):
- class StreamingChatSession:
    - __init__(client, model, stream_id=None, options=None)
    - async def start(self): returns an AsyncIterator[Event] (events = token/fragment, tool_call, safety, meta)
    - def on_event(self, fn): register callback for Event objects
    - async def checkpoint(self) -> str: produce a short resume token (base64)
    - async def resume(self, resume_token: str) -> AsyncIterator[Event]: resume a partially consumed stream from the checkpoint if the runtime supports resumability
    - async def finalize(self): mark session as completed (flushes caches and emits final telemetry)

Event model (flattened concept):
- Event.type in {"token", "fragment", "tool_call", "safety", "meta", "end"}
- Event.payload: string (for token/fragment/tool), dict-ish string for structured events (JSON string).
- Event.offset: monotonically increasing integer for ordering; included in checkpoint state.

Resumable semantics:
- Server provides event offsets and can optionally sign a checkpoint. SDK's checkpoint() will return a resume token composed of: model-version|stream-id|offset|short-hmac. SDK verifies signature when resuming.
- If resume verification fails (signature mismatch or missing), SDK will surface a deterministic RetryNeeded error with contextual telemetry.
- Resume should not re-deliver any committed tokens. Committed tokens are those where the app called checkpoint() or that were behind an explicit 'commit' meta event from the server.

Safety behavior and UX guidelines for apps:
- Safety events are delivered as separate Event.type == 'safety' with fields: reason, severity (info|warn|block), snippet_offsets (optional).
- Default SDK behavior: buffer tokens until the safety event is resolved. Expose two config modes: "eager_render" (developer takes responsibility; SDK emits tokens promptly) and "conservative" (SDK buffers until safe).
- If safety.severity == 'block', SDK should emit a stream-abort meta-event and provide a resume token pointing at the last safe checkpoint; the app can surface a fallback or request an alternative model.

Backward compatibility mapping:
- Legacy token events without types are mapped to Event.type == 'token'. Legacy 'moderation' envelopes are mapped to 'safety'. For servers that do not yet provide signed checkpoints, SDK will fallback to conservative client-side checkpointing (best-effort resume with warning telemetry).

Testing and validation plan:
- Unit tests for event-layer mapping (legacy -> new events).
- Integration test harness that simulates: normal stream, mid-stream safety block, network interruption with resume success, resume failure (signature mismatch), duplicate suppression. Use pytest-asyncio.
- Fuzz test generator to emit interleaved tokens, tool calls, and safety events to ensure SDK ordering guarantees hold.
- Telemetry tests to validate metrics: safety_trigger_count, resume_success_rate, duplicate_suppressed_count.

Acceptance criteria (must pass to mark Done):
1) SDK exposes StreamingChatSession API and async iterator usage documented in README with examples.
2) Checkpoint tokens are verifiable; resume tests pass for both signed and best-effort modes.
3) Safety events are emitted as separate events and developer-configurable buffering modes work.
4) No new latency regression >5% for median token latency in throughput test.
5) Tests covering edge cases (resume after block, duplicate stream prevention) and telemetry assertions included.
6) PR with implementation and unit+integration tests merged; docs page added to SDK streaming ergonomics guide.

Rollout and migration plan:
- Feature flagged release: server-side support behind a runtime flag 'streaming-safety-v2'. SDK will default to compatibility mode and opt into new behavior if server advertises checkpoint/signing capability.
- Beta release to selected customers (internal and 3 external partners) for two weeks. Collect failures via telemetry and roll-forward fixes.
- After stable beta, flip default for new SDK versions and publish migration notes.

Implementation notes and trade-offs considered:
- Option A: Full transcript signing at each token would give stronger guarantees but is too expensive; chosen opt: short incremental signed offsets to stay lightweight.
- Option B: Server-only safety resolution (server swallows blocked tokens) reduces SDK complexity but hides important developer control; chosen opt: surface safety events to let app decide UX.

Documentation and examples to land with the change:
- docs/python/streaming_guide.md: new sections 'Safety events', 'Resumable streams', 'Checkpointing example'.
- Examples in repo: examples/stream_resume_demo.py showing resume use-cases, and examples/stream_safety_policy.py demonstrating conservative vs eager modes.

updates: 2026-03-12: Initial design and API sketched during SDK sync; owner: Maya. Decision to expose explicit safety events and not swallow blocked content made after discussion with product.
2026-03-13: Prototyped StreamingChatSession.checkpoint() that encodes offset and stream-id; prototype PR created: github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-python-sdk/pull/5342 (draft).

2026-03-14: Meeting with runtime team — they agreed to add optional signed checkpoint header 'X-Stream-Checkpoint' behind flag streaming-safety-v2. Updated dependency list. Starting integration tests.
